cards.claim: Regularization strength should scale with image resolution during progressive training
cards.conditions: ImageNet ILSVRC2012, single model architecture tested at different resolutions with varying augmentation magnitudes
cards.effect: At size 128: RandAug mag 5 achieves 78.3%; at size 300: RandAug mag 15 achieves 83.2%. Weak augmentation (mag 5) at size 300 gives only 82.5%.
cards.evidence: Table 5 showing accuracy at different image sizes (128, 192, 300) with RandAugment magnitudes (5, 10, 15), plus motivation text in Section 4.1
cards.quote: for the same network, smaller image size leads to smaller network capacity and thus needs weaker regularization; vice versa, larger image size leads to more computations with larger capacity, and thus more vulnerable to overfitting

cards.claim: Training with smaller image sizes and weak regularization in early stages, then increasing both during later training stages, enables faster training without accuracy loss
cards.conditions: ImageNet ILSVRC2012, 350 epochs divided into 4 stages (~87 epochs each), EfficientNetV2-S/M/L models
cards.effect: EfficientNetV2 models achieve state-of-the-art accuracy (85.7% top-1 for L) while training 3x-9x faster than previous models; progressive learning eliminates the accuracy drop typically seen in prior progressive resizing approaches
cards.evidence: Table 7 results, Table 6 showing progressive learning schedule, Section 4.2 algorithm and results discussion
cards.quote: in the early training epochs, we train the network with smaller images and weak regularization, such that the network can learn simple representations easily and fast. Then, we gradually increase image size but also making learning more difficult by adding stronger regularization

cards.claim: FixRes (using smaller training image size than inference size) speeds up training substantially while maintaining or improving accuracy
cards.conditions: EfficientNet-B6 on ImageNet, TPUv3 cores, comparing train_size=512 vs train_size=380, varying batch sizes (32, 128)
cards.effect: Training throughput improves by up to 2.2x (from 42 to 76 imgs/sec on TPUv3 with batch=32); accuracy improves from 84.3% to 84.6%
cards.evidence: Table 2 showing throughput and accuracy for different image sizes and batch sizes
cards.quote: smaller image size leads to less computations and enables large batch size, and thus improves training speed by up to 2.2x. Notably, as pointed out in (Touvron et al., 2020 ; Brock et al., 2021), using smaller image size for training also leads to slightly better accuracy

cards.claim: Progressive increasing of image resolution during training is a valid approach but requires corresponding regularization adjustment to avoid accuracy drop
cards.conditions: ImageNet ILSVRC2012, ConvNet training with variable resolution schedules
cards.effect: Previous works (progressive resizing, Mix&Match) that increased resolution without adjusting regularization caused accuracy drops; EfficientNetV2 with adaptive regularization eliminates this
cards.evidence: Section 4.1 motivation and discussion of prior work, comparison of results with/without progressive learning
cards.quote: Previous works have proposed different kinds of progressive training, which dynamically change the training settings or networks, for GANs (Karras et al., 2018), transfer learning (Karras et al., 2018), adversarial learning (Yu et al., 2019), and language models (Press et al., 2021). Progressive resizing (Howard, 2018) is mostly related to our approach, which aims to improve training speed. However, it usually comes with the cost of accuracy drop

cards.claim: Dropout rate should increase with training image resolution during progressive learning
cards.conditions: EfficientNetV2-S/M/L on ImageNet, 350-epoch training schedule divided into 4 stages
cards.effect: EfficientNetV2-S uses dropout 0.1→0.3; M uses 0.1→0.4; L uses 0.1→0.5. Larger models that train at larger resolutions require stronger dropout.
cards.evidence: Table 6 showing progressive training settings (min/max image size and regularization values) for each model size
cards.quote: For simplicity, all models use the same minimum values of size and regularization, but they adopt different maximum values, as larger models generally require more regularization to combat overfitting

cards.claim: Mixup ratio should increase with training image resolution during progressive learning
cards.effect: EfficientNetV2-S uses mixup 0→0; M uses 0→0.2; L uses 0→0.4. Larger models training at larger resolutions benefit from stronger mixup augmentation.
cards.evidence: Table 6 progressive learning schedule for mixup alpha parameter
cards.quote: Table 6 : Progressive training settings for EfficientNetV2. S M L min max min max min max... Mixup alpha 0 0 0 0.2 0 0.4

cards.claim: RandAugment magnitude should increase with training image resolution
cards.conditions: EfficientNetV2-S/M/L on ImageNet, 350-epoch training with 4 progressive stages
cards.effect: EfficientNetV2-S uses RandAugment 5→15; M uses 5→20; L uses 5→25. Larger models at larger resolutions require stronger augmentation.
cards.evidence: Table 6 showing RandAugment magnitude schedule; Table 5 empirical validation of augmentation magnitude vs image size
cards.quote: Table 6 : Progressive training settings for EfficientNetV2... RandAugment 5 15 5 20 5 25

cards.claim: Batch norm weights can be directly transferred when changing image resolution during progressive training
cards.conditions: ConvNet architecture, weight inheritance between training stages
cards.effect: Enables seamless transition between resolution stages without reinitialization
cards.quote: Unlike transformers, whose weights (e.g., position embedding) may depend on input length, ConvNet weights are independent to image sizes and thus can be inherited easily

cards.claim: Linear interpolation is a simple and effective method for scheduling regularization across training stages
cards.conditions: ImageNet ILSVRC2012, EfficientNetV2 models with 4 training stages
cards.effect: Achieves state-of-the-art results on ImageNet with no reported degradation
cards.evidence: Algorithm 1 and Section 4.2 description of the progressive learning procedure
cards.quote: For simplicity, we heuristically pick the initial image size and regularization, and then use a linear interpolation to determine the value for each stage
